title: Intel confirms Nova Lake on 18A-P as server demand reshapes factory plans
gist: Intel confirmed Nova Lake as its first client family on 18A-P (claimed +9% performance or -18% power vs 18A), running ahead of schedule with launch design wins expected at 2x Panther Lake. Meanwhile Intel is converting some Oregon 18A capacity meant for Panther Lake to Intel 3 to supply Granite Rapids server CPUs, since AI-driven server demand exceeds supply while PCs weaken on memory costs.

insights.claim: Intel confirmed Nova Lake will be its first client processor family on the enhanced Intel 18A-P process, with more details due at CES in January 2027.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Validates 18A-P as a production node for Intel's next client cycle.
insights.quote: Nova Lake will be its first client processor family to use the enhanced Intel 18A-P manufacturing process
insights.locator: Intel has confirmed that Nova Lake

insights.claim: CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Nova Lake is progressing ahead of schedule and expects launch design wins at twice those of Panther Lake, signalling broader OEM adoption.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Potential client share/ASP tailwind for Intel in 2027 if execution holds.
insights.quote: expected design wins at launch would be twice those of Panther Lake

insights.claim: Intel claims 18A-P delivers 9% higher performance at the same power or 18% lower power at equal performance versus 18A, via transistor, interconnect and design-optimisation improvements, but these are process-level figures, not confirmed Nova Lake product gains.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Discount node-level PPA claims when modelling product competitiveness.
insights.quote: Intel claims nine percent higher performance at the same power, or 18 percent lower power at equivalent performance.

insights.claim: It is not established that every Nova Lake tile will be made on Intel's own process; manufacturing allocations remain undisclosed, so external foundry use is still possible.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Key open question for Intel Foundry volume and any TSMC exposure; watch CES.
insights.quote: The announcement does not establish that every Nova Lake tile will use Intel’s process.

insights.claim: CFO Dave Zinsner said some Oregon capacity intended for 18A-based Panther Lake will be taken offline and converted to Intel 3 to support more data-centre output, becoming productive in 2H 2027.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Intel reallocates fab capacity toward higher-demand server CPUs; relief arrives only in 2H27.
insights.quote: some Oregon capacity intended for 18A-based Panther Lake chips would be taken offline and converted to Intel 3 production

insights.claim: Granite Rapids is built on Intel 3 and is among Intel's fastest-ramping server products, with server demand still exceeding available supply.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Server CPU supply-constrained through 2027 implies pricing power for Intel DCAI.
insights.quote: while server demand continues to exceed available supply

insights.claim: Diverging end-markets drive the shift: AI infrastructure is strengthening server CPU demand, while expensive memory and constrained budgets are weakening PC purchases.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: AI buildout lifts general-purpose CPU demand while memory cost inflation hurts PC units.
insights.quote: AI infrastructure is strengthening demand for server CPUs, while expensive memory and constrained customer budgets are weakening PC purchases

insights.claim: As of November 2026 three Intel processor families ship on original 18A, while two more announced families use 18A-P: Nova Lake for client and Diamond Rapids for servers.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Gauge of 18A-family adoption breadth across client and server.
insights.quote: Two additional announced families use the enhanced 18A-P process: Nova Lake for client PCs and Diamond Rapids for servers.
